function: U-nets learn discrete UL and DL IRS phase shifts from CSI; DRL learns UAV hover location, DL/UL time allocation and multi-UAV scheduling to minimize system energy (pp. 6-9).
system: Single-antenna devices and MUAVs; M AUAVs each carrying a reflecting 8x8 IRS with 8 phase levels; narrow-band LoS links, 180 kHz; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3-5, 11).
method: U-net with quantization layer, unsupervised (loss: negative channel gain or rate); off-policy reinforcement learning: SAC with PTI for trajectory, D3QN with action mask for scheduling (pp. 6-10).
data_channel: Custom simulator: LoS narrow-band IRS channel [12], d^-2 path loss, perfect CSI, small-scale fading compensated; unlabeled CSI samples drawn at random UAV and device locations (pp. 4, 6).
test_conditions: U-net trained on CSI sampled over all subareas, tested on Xtest (generation not detailed); one DRL actor trained per subarea; Sk in [45,55] Mb (pp. 7, 8, 11).
baselines: Non-learned: IRS off, PTI heuristic trajectories; learned: SAC, DDPG, pure joint SAC; own variants CPO, CPOD, DPO-P; HMCS without AUAVs (pp. 11, 12, 14).
metrics: DL mean sum of unit power channel gains; UL unit-bandwidth sum rate; accumulated reward; system energy, task completion time, traveling energy, recharging times (pp. 11, 12, 14).
complexity: Table V: P1a/P1b 51.72 Mb, 26.93 MFLOPs, 2.42 ms; P2 2.54 Mb, 3.42 MFLOPs, 0.04 ms; P3 3.02-3.79 Mb, 7.30-13.39 MFLOPs (RTX 2080Ti, p. 14).
q1_support: p. 4: "According to the classical narrow-band reflection channel model [12]"; p. 4: "the small-scale fading is assumed to be perfectly compensated"
q2_support: p. 8: "a specialized actor network must be trained for each subarea"; p. 7: "we can expand the data set by randomly generating CSI from all the subareas"
q3_support: p. 11: "we also provide the performance lower bounds when the IRS is turned off"; p. 11: "as two baseline methods to solve P2"; p. 1: "improve performance by more than 90% compared to the pure DRL method"
q4_support: p. 14: "in terms of parameter size, million floating-point operations (MFLOPs)"
q5_support: p. 6: "we constantly sample wU from W to generate nonrepetitive data set with a finite size"
notes: Included: the U-nets learn IRS phase shifts (physical layer) and the DRL agents learn time allocation, hover location and scheduling (pp. 6-10), so above_phy does not apply. Area 6 rather than 3: the learned IRS-phase and time-allocation control serves UAV (aerial) links, and 6 precedes 3 in the Step 2 order; the U-net alone would be area 3 (RIS phase shifts). q1=0: custom LoS simulator with perfect CSI, no 3GPP, DeepMIMO or measured channel (p. 4). q2=0: the paper never tests a model on an unseen scenario; actors are trained per subarea (p. 8), the P3 network size depends on the number of MUAVs (p. 14), so Table IV looks like per-condition retraining. q3=1 is a judgement: non-learned references are IRS off (Table III, p. 11) and the PTI heuristic trajectories (Fig. 8(a), p. 12); learned baselines are SAC and DDPG applied to the same problem (p. 11) and the pure joint SAC of the abstract, while CPO, CPOD and DPO-P are variants of the method and do not count. q4=1: Table V (p. 14) gives parameter size, MFLOPs and decision time. q5=0: no code or data link; data are simulated (p. 6).
